title: Activation Energy Determination – Arrhenius Plot Builder
prompt:
Create a single HTML file using Three.js that simulates a chemistry lab for determining activation energy via the Arrhenius equation. The scene must expose all state on window.__3D_STATE__.

## Scene Setup
- Use a perspective camera at position (0, 5, 12) looking at origin.
- Add ambient light (intensity 0.4) and a directional light from (5, 10, 5) with intensity 0.8.
- Render a 3D lab bench (box geometry, wood-brown color, ~10x0.3x4) centered at y=0.
- On the bench, place a 3D beaker (cylinder, transparent blue-tinted glass material, radius 0.6, height 1.5) at position (-2, 0.9, 0). Inside the beaker, place a colored liquid (shorter cylinder, orange, radius 0.55) whose height represents reaction progress.
- Place a 3D thermometer object next to the beaker (thin cylinder, red inner tube whose height changes with temperature).
- Place a 3D stopwatch object on the right side of the bench (flat cylinder with a clock face texture or simple circle with text).
- Use OrbitControls for camera rotation.

## Arrhenius Chemistry Model
- The Arrhenius equation: k = A * exp(-Ea / (R * T)), where A = 1e13 s^-1 (pre-exponential factor), Ea is the true activation energy = 75000 J/mol (75 kJ/mol), R = 8.314 J/(mol·K), T is temperature in Kelvin.
- The reaction rate constant k determines how fast the liquid level drops in the beaker during a trial run.
- Maintain an array of experimental data points: each entry is { temperature: T_in_K, rateConstant: k_measured, inv_T: 1000/T, ln_k: Math.log(k) }.

## Temperature Control
- Display a DOM panel on the left side with:
  - A label showing current temperature in °C and K.
  - Two buttons: '+10°C' and '-10°C' to adjust temperature (range: 20°C to 120°C, i.e., 293K to 393K). Default: 25°C (298K).
  - A 'Run Reaction' button that starts a trial at the current temperature.
  - A 'Record Data Point' button (enabled only after a reaction run completes).
  - A 'Calculate Ea' button (enabled only when >= 3 data points are recorded).
  - A 'Reset All' button to clear all data and reset.

## Reaction Simulation
- When 'Run Reaction' is clicked, compute k = A * exp(-Ea / (R * T)) for the current T.
- Animate the liquid level in the beaker dropping from full (height 1.2) to empty (height 0.1) over a duration inversely proportional to k (use duration = clamp(0.5 / k * 1e10, 1.0, 8.0) seconds so it's visible).
- The thermometer's red inner tube height should reflect the current temperature (scale linearly from 293K->0.2 to 393K->1.4).
- While the reaction runs, the stopwatch should animate a timer showing elapsed seconds.
- Set window.__3D_STATE__.reactionRunning = true during animation, false when done.
- After the reaction completes, store the measured rate constant and set window.__3D_STATE__.lastMeasuredK = k.

## Data Recording & Arrhenius Plot
- When 'Record Data Point' is clicked, push { temperature, rateConstant, inv_T: 1000/T, ln_k: Math.log(k) } into the data array.
- Display a 2D Arrhenius plot on a DOM canvas (400x300px) on the right side of the screen:
  - X-axis: 1000/T (K^-1), range roughly 2.5 to 3.5.
  - Y-axis: ln(k), auto-scaled to data.
  - Plot each recorded data point as a red circle.
  - When >= 2 points exist, draw a best-fit line (linear regression on 1000/T vs ln(k)).
- Update the plot each time a new data point is recorded.

## Activation Energy Calculation
- When 'Calculate Ea' is clicked (>= 3 data points):
  - Perform linear regression: ln(k) = -Ea/(R*1000) * (1000/T) + ln(A). The slope m = -Ea / (R * 1000), so Ea_calculated = -m * R * 1000.
  - Store the calculated Ea and display it on the DOM panel: 'Calculated Ea: XX.X kJ/mol'.
  - Also display the percentage error vs true Ea (75 kJ/mol).
  - Highlight the best-fit line on the Arrhenius plot in green.
  - Set window.__3D_STATE__.calculatedEa = Ea_calculated (in J/mol).
  - Set window.__3D_STATE__.percentageError = Math.abs(Ea_calculated - 75000) / 75000 * 100.

## State Management (window.__3D_STATE__)
Expose and keep updated:
- temperatureC: current temperature in Celsius (number)
- temperatureK: current temperature in Kelvin (number)
- reactionRunning: boolean
- lastMeasuredK: last computed rate constant (number or null)
- dataPoints: array of recorded { temperature, rateConstant, inv_T, ln_k } objects
- dataPointCount: number of recorded data points
- calculatedEa: calculated activation energy in J/mol (number or null)
- percentageError: percentage error vs true Ea (number or null)
- trueEa: 75000 (constant)
- liquidLevel: current liquid height in beaker (number, 0.1 to 1.2)
- thermometerLevel: current thermometer red tube height (number)
- regressionSlope: slope from linear regression (number or null)
- regressionIntercept: intercept from linear regression (number or null)
- plotRendered: boolean, true after plot canvas has been drawn at least once
- reactionCompleted: boolean, true after at least one reaction has finished
- stopwatchTime: elapsed time in seconds during last/current reaction run (number)

## Visual Polish
- Add a subtle grid helper on the floor below the bench.
- The beaker liquid should have slight transparency.
- Use a clean dark background (#1a1a2e).
- DOM panels should have semi-transparent dark backgrounds with white text, rounded corners.
physics_constraints: Arrhenius equation k = A*exp(-Ea/(R*T)) with A=1e13, Ea=75000 J/mol, R=8.314. Rate constant must be strictly positive and increase monotonically with temperature. ln(k) vs 1000/T must be linear. Calculated Ea from regression on clean data must converge to 75000 J/mol within <1% error. Temperature bounded [293K, 393K]. Liquid level bounded [0.1, 1.2]. All numerical values must be NaN-free and finite.
